1.description: While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seed on its back in order to grow.
1.name: Bulbasaur

10.description: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.
10.name: Caterpie

100.description: An enigmatic Pokémon that happens to bear a resemblance to a Poké Ball. When excited, it discharges the electric current it has stored in its belly, then lets out a great, uproarious laugh.
100.name: Voltorb

1000.description: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.
1000.name: Gholdengo

1001.description: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.
1001.name: Wo-Chien

1002.description: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.
1002.name: Chien-Pao

1003.description: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.
1003.name: Ting-Lu

1004.description: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.
1004.name: Chi-Yu

1005.description: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.
1005.name: Roaring Moon

1006.description: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.
1006.name: Iron Valiant

1007.description: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.
1007.name: Koraidon

1008.description: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.
1008.name: Miraidon

1009.description: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.
1009.name: Walking Wake

101.description: The tissue on the surface of its body is curiously similar in composition to an Apricorn. When irritated, this Pokémon lets loose an electric current equal to 20 lightning bolts.
101.name: Electrode

1010.description: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.
1010.name: Iron Leaves

1011.description: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.
1011.name: Dipplin

1012.description: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.
1012.name: Poltchageist

1013.description: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.
1013.name: Sinistcha

1014.description: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.
1014.name: Okidogi

1015.description: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.
1015.name: Munkidori

1016.description: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.
1016.name: Fezandipiti

1017.description: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.
1017.name: Ogerpon

1018.description: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.
1018.name: Archaludon

1019.description: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.
1019.name: Hydrapple

102.description: These Pokémon get nervous when they’re not in a group of six. The minute even one member of the group goes missing, Exeggcute become cowardly.
102.name: Exeggcute

1020.description: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.
1020.name: Gouging Fire

1021.description: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.
1021.name: Raging Bolt

1022.description: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.
1022.name: Iron Boulder

1023.description: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.
1023.name: Iron Crown

1024.description: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.
1024.name: Terapagos

1025.description: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
1025.name: Pecharunt

103.description: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.
103.name: Exeggutor

104.description: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.
104.name: Cubone

105.description: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.
105.name: Marowak

106.description: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.
106.name: Hitmonlee

107.description: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.
107.name: Hitmonchan

108.description: Wields its long tongue deftly, as though it were an arm. The Pokémon's viscous saliva, once it has been collected and boiled down, yields a strong and highly useful adhesive.
108.name: Lickitung

109.description: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.
109.name: Koffing

11.description: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.
11.name: Metapod

110.description: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.
110.name: Weezing

111.description: Ludicrously strong—when it butts heads with a mountain, it is the mountain that shatters. But its short legs struggle with turns, and it is incapable of stopping unless it collides with something.
111.name: Rhyhorn

112.description: Rapidly rotates its horn to bore through bedrock. It swaggers around volcanic regions, protected from the lava's heat by its tough, armorlike hide.
112.name: Rhydon

113.description: This purehearted Pokémon shares its eggs with the injured.
113.name: Chansey

114.description: It is cloaked entirely in blue vines, preventing any glimpse of its true identity. The vines impart a refreshing sensation when chewed—they're useful as a spice.
114.name: Tangela

115.description: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.
115.name: Kangaskhan

116.description: They swim with dance-like motions and cause whirlpools to form. Horsea compete to see which of them can generate the biggest whirlpool.
116.name: Horsea

117.description: Seadra’s mouth is slender, but its suction power is strong. In an instant, Seadra can suck in food that’s larger than the opening of its mouth.
117.name: Seadra

118.description: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.
118.name: Goldeen

119.description: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.
119.name: Seaking

12.description: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.
12.name: Butterfree

120.description: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn’t bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.
120.name: Staryu

121.description: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.
121.name: Starmie

122.description: The behavior of this clown-like Pokémon reminds one of pantomime. It creates invisible walls using a force emitted from its fingertips.
122.name: Mr. Mime

123.description: The large, wickedly sharp scythes on its forearms are truly fearsome weapons. Prey's attempts to flee are unfailingly thwarted by this Pokémon's nimble motions.
123.name: Scyther

124.description: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.
124.name: Jynx

125.description: Feeds on electrical energy. During sudden showers beneath looming thunderclouds, one can observe Electabuzz scaling tall trees, where the Pokémon will then wait for lightning to strike.
125.name: Electabuzz

126.description: Legend has it that this Pokémon was born from the crater of a volcano. When wounded, it bathes in lava to heal its body, much as one would soak in a hot spring.
126.name: Magmar

127.description: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.
127.name: Pinsir

128.description: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.
128.name: Tauros

129.description: A feeble, pitiful imbecile of a Pokémon that is nonetheless very hardy. Unperturbed by turbid water, it can be found living in all sorts of places.
129.name: Magikarp

13.description: Beware of the sharp stinger on its head. It hides in grass and bushes where it eats leaves.
13.name: Weedle

130.description: I suspect this Pokémon to be the true identity of a dragon written of in ancient texts, which claimed that it razed an entire village with white-hot beams from its maw.
130.name: Gyarados

131.description: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.
131.name: Lapras

132.description: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.
132.name: Ditto

133.description: Harbors the potential to evolve into manifold forms. Within Eevee lies the key to the mysteries of Pokémon evolution—I'm certain of it.
133.name: Eevee

134.description: Tests show that its cells closely resemble water molecules, which perhaps explains its ability to conceal its form while submerged. I believe the origins of mermaid folklore lie with this Pokémon.
134.name: Vaporeon

135.description: Bristles its fur into sharp, needlelike points when enraged. One can hear electricity crackle in its breath when it exhales.
135.name: Jolteon

136.description: Flames burn within a saclike organ inside this Pokémon. When Flareon inhales, these flames grow in intensity, reaching a mighty 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.
136.name: Flareon

137.description: It has no discernible heartbeat and does not seem to draw breath, and yet it appears to function without issue. I cannot even begin to explain this utterly bizarre anomaly.
137.name: Porygon

138.description: This Pokémon is a member of an ancient, extinct species. Omanyte paddles through water with its 10 tentacles, looking like it’s just drifting along.
138.name: Omanyte

139.description: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.
139.name: Omastar

14.description: Able to move only slightly. When endangered, it may stick out its stinger and poison its enemy.
14.name: Kakuna

140.description: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.
140.name: Kabuto

141.description: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.
141.name: Kabutops

142.description: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.
142.name: Aerodactyl

143.description: This glutton appears in villages without warning and devours the entirety of their rice granaries—such occurrences have long been counted among the gravest of disasters.
143.name: Snorlax

144.description: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.
144.name: Articuno

145.description: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.
145.name: Zapdos

146.description: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.
146.name: Moltres

147.description: This Pokémon was long considered to be no more than a myth. The small lump on a Dratini’s forehead is actually a horn that’s still coming in.
147.name: Dratini

148.description: This Pokémon gathers power in the orbs on its tail and controls the weather. When enshrouded by an aura, Dragonair has a mystical appearance.
148.name: Dragonair

149.description: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.
149.name: Dragonite

15.description: It has three poisonous stingers on its forelegs and its tail. They are used to jab its enemy repeatedly.
15.name: Beedrill

150.description: Its DNA is almost the same as Mew’s. However, its size and disposition are vastly different.
150.name: Mewtwo

151.description: When viewed through a microscope, this Pokémon’s short, fine, delicate hair can be seen.
151.name: Mew

152.description: In battle, Chikorita waves its leaf around to keep the foe at bay. However, a sweet fragrance also wafts from the leaf, becalming the battling Pokémon and creating a cozy, friendly atmosphere all around.
152.name: Chikorita

153.description: Bayleef’s neck is ringed by curled-up leaves. Inside each tubular leaf is a small shoot of a tree. The fragrance of this shoot makes people peppy.
153.name: Bayleef

154.description: The fragrance of Meganium’s flower soothes and calms emotions. In battle, this Pokémon gives off more of its becalming scent to blunt the foe’s fighting spirit.
154.name: Meganium

155.description: Hails from the Johto region. Though usually curled into a ball due to its timid disposition, it harbors tremendous firepower.
155.name: Cyndaquil

156.description: This creature's fur is most mysterious—it is wholly impervious to the burning touch of flame. Should Quilava turn its back to you, take heed! Such a posture indicates a forthcoming attack.
156.name: Quilava

157.description: Said to purify lost, forsaken souls with its flames and guide them to the afterlife. I believe its form has been influenced by the energy of the sacred mountain towering at Hisui's center.
157.name: Typhlosion

158.description: Despite the smallness of its body, Totodile’s jaws are very powerful. While the Pokémon may think it is just playfully nipping, its bite has enough power to cause serious injury.
158.name: Totodile

159.description: Once Croconaw has clamped its jaws on its foe, it will absolutely not let go. Because the tips of its fangs are forked back like barbed fishhooks, they become impossible to remove when they have sunk in.
159.name: Croconaw

16.description: Very docile. If attacked, it will often kick up sand to protect itself rather than fight back.
16.name: Pidgey

160.description: Feraligatr intimidates its foes by opening its huge mouth. In battle, it will kick the ground hard with its thick and powerful hind legs to charge at the foe at an incredible speed.
160.name: Feraligatr

161.description: When Sentret sleeps, it does so while another stands guard. The sentry wakes the others at the first sign of danger. When this Pokémon becomes separated from its pack, it becomes incapable of sleep due to fear.
161.name: Sentret

162.description: Furret has a very slim build. When under attack, it can slickly squirm through narrow spaces and get away. In spite of its short limbs, this Pokémon is very nimble and fleet.
162.name: Furret

163.description: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.
163.name: Hoothoot

164.description: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.
164.name: Noctowl

165.description: These very cowardly Pokémon join together and use Reflect to protect their nest.
165.name: Ledyba

166.description: It flies through the night sky, sprinkling sparkly dust. According to some, if that dust sticks to you, good things will happen to you.
166.name: Ledian

167.description: Although the poison from its fangs isn’t that strong, it’s potent enough to weaken prey that gets caught in its web.
167.name: Spinarak

168.description: It spews threads from its mouth to catch its prey. When night falls, it leaves its web to go hunt aggressively.
168.name: Ariados

169.description: Its hind limbs have become another set of wings. Crobat expertly maneuvers its four wings to dart in exquisite fashion through even the most confined caves without losing any speed.
169.name: Crobat

17.description: This Pokémon is full of vitality. It constantly flies around its large territory in search of prey.
17.name: Pidgeotto

170.description: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.
170.name: Chinchou

171.description: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.
171.name: Lanturn

172.description: Pichu stores electricity in the sacs on its cheeks but discharges it inadvertently when agitated or excited. Being yet immature, the Pokémon's handling of electricity is rather inept.
172.name: Pichu

173.description: In silhouette, they resemble twinkling starlight. When shooting stars rain from the night sky, Cleffa gather in numbers and dance as though they are indeed incarnations of the stars.
173.name: Cleffa

174.description: Taking advantage of the softness of its body, Igglybuff moves as if bouncing. Its body turns a deep pink when its temperature rises.
174.name: Igglybuff

175.description: This ovate creature is frequently mistaken for a moving egg when encountered out in the fields or in the mountains. Its guileless smile soothes the soul.
175.name: Togepi

176.description: No records exist of Togetic being seen in the wilds. Rumors abound that it evolves under the loving care of a trusted human companion, upon whom the Pokémon then bestows great joy.
176.name: Togetic

177.description: Because its wings aren’t yet fully grown, it has to hop to get around. It is always staring at something.
177.name: Natu

178.description: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.
178.name: Xatu

179.description: Rubbing its fleece generates electricity. You’ll want to pet it because it’s cute, but if you use your bare hand, you’ll get a painful shock.
179.name: Mareep

18.description: This Pokémon flies at Mach 2 speed, seeking prey. Its large talons are feared as wicked weapons.
18.name: Pidgeot

180.description: It stores electricity in its fluffy fleece. If it stores up too much, it will start to go bald in those patches.
180.name: Flaaffy

181.description: Its tail shines bright and strong. It has been prized since long ago as a beacon for sailors.
181.name: Ampharos

182.description: Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.
182.name: Bellossom

183.description: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water- repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That’s why this Pokémon is never cold.
183.name: Marill

184.description: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.
184.name: Azumarill

185.description: Though it pretends to be a tree, it fails to fool even children. To the touch, its body feels more like rock than tree bark. Sudowoodo's extreme aversion to water merits special note.
185.name: Sudowoodo

186.description: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.
186.name: Politoed

187.description: This Pokémon drifts and floats with the wind. If it senses the approach of strong winds, Hoppip links its leaves with other Hoppip to prepare against being blown away.
187.name: Hoppip

188.description: Skiploom’s flower blossoms when the temperature rises above 64 degrees Fahrenheit. How much the flower opens depends on the temperature. For that reason, this Pokémon is sometimes used as a thermometer.
188.name: Skiploom

189.description: Jumpluff rides warm southern winds to cross the sea and fly to foreign lands. The Pokémon descends to the ground when it encounters cold air while it is floating.
189.name: Jumpluff

19.description: Will chew on anything with its fangs. If you see one, you can be certain that 40 more live in the area.
19.name: Rattata

190.description: This treetop dweller possesses a tail as dexterous as a hand. Ancient writings describe this Pokémon as a one-armed oddity.
190.name: Aipom

191.description: Sunkern tries to move as little as it possibly can. It does so because it tries to conserve all the nutrients it has stored in its body for its evolution. It will not eat a thing, subsisting only on morning dew.
191.name: Sunkern

192.description: Sunflora converts solar energy into nutrition. It moves around actively in the daytime when it is warm. It stops moving as soon as the sun goes down for the night.
192.name: Sunflora

193.description: Its frail wings are so thin that one can see clear through them. However, during flight these wings exhibit the power to churn air with force enough to launch a house skyward.
193.name: Yanma

194.description: When walking on land, it covers its body with a poisonous film that keeps its skin from dehydrating.
194.name: Wooper

195.description: Its body is always slimy. It often bangs its head on the river bottom as it swims but seems not to care.
195.name: Quagsire

196.description: Wields an arcane power with which it can predict the weather and even people's thoughts. When bathed in sunshine, the scarlet orb on its brow glows and builds energy.
196.name: Espeon

197.description: It is most active in the wee hours of the night, when moonlight bathes the land. Its large eyes can pierce the darkness and perceive prey with absolute clarity.
197.name: Umbreon

198.description: Widely shunned as a bearer of ill fortune. Upon crossing paths with this creature, I've been told one must chant ”Workrum, Workrum—bad luck, don't come” as a protective incantation.
198.name: Murkrow

199.description: Slowking can solve any problem presented to it, but no one can understand a thing Slowking says.
199.name: Slowking

2.description: Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.
2.name: Ivysaur

20.description: Its hind feet are webbed. They act as flippers, so it can swim in rivers and hunt for prey.
20.name: Raticate

200.description: It conceals itself in darkness, sending chills up travelers' spines with its childlike weeping. As it observes the frightened travelers with glee, the red orbs upon its chest let off an eerie light.
200.name: Misdreavus

201.description: It is hard to believe these strangely shaped Pokémon are truly living creatures. I've pointed out that the species' many forms resemble writing from other lands; no one will take me seriously.
201.name: Unown

202.description: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.
202.name: Wobbuffet

203.description: Girafarig’s rear head contains a tiny brain that is too small for thinking. However, the rear head doesn’t need to sleep, so it can keep watch over its surroundings 24 hours a day.
203.name: Girafarig

204.description: It sticks tree bark to itself with its saliva, making itself thicker and larger. Elderly Pineco are ridiculously huge.
204.name: Pineco

205.description: In the moment that it gulps down its prey, the inside of its shell is exposed, but to this day, no one has ever seen that sight.
205.name: Forretress

206.description: The nests Dunsparce live in are mazes of tunnels. They never get lost in their own nests—they can tell where they are by the scent of the dirt.
206.name: Dunsparce

207.description: Its tail is tipped by a thick, horrible stinger. To bring down prey, it will first obscure their vision by covering their faces with its body, and then it will use the stinger to inject them with venom.
207.name: Gligar

208.description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a strange item. Its body is coated with steel powder and notably hard—not even diamond can leave so much as a scratch.
208.name: Steelix

209.description: In contrast to its appearance, it’s quite timid. When playing with other puppy Pokémon, it sometimes gets bullied.
209.name: Snubbull

21.description: Inept at flying high. However, it can fly around very fast to protect its territory.
21.name: Spearow

210.description: Although it’s popular with young people, Granbull is timid and sensitive, so it’s totally incompetent as a watchdog.
210.name: Granbull

211.description: Fishers detest this troublesome Pokémon because it sprays poison from its spines, getting it everywhere. A different form of Qwilfish lives in other regions.
211.name: Qwilfish

212.description: Evolved by way of a curious item. The shell covering its body has been shown to be stronger than forged steel.
212.name: Scizor

213.description: The berries stored in its vaselike shell eventually become a thick, pulpy juice.
213.name: Shuckle

214.description: This Pokémon has an unparalleled horn. Heracross itself demonstrates tremendous power—it's capable of throwing several people trained in the traditional arts of war at once.
214.name: Heracross

215.description: Its sturdy, curved claws are ideal for traversing precipitous cliffs. From the tips of these claws drips a venom that infiltrates the nerves of any prey caught in Sneasel's grasp.
215.name: Sneasel

216.description: It licks its paws because of the sweet honey that has soaked into them. It is cunning, stealing into the nests of Combee and taking for itself the honey that the Combee have amassed.
216.name: Teddiursa

217.description: When the cold season arrives in Hisui, this Pokémon will wander fields and mountains alike in search of its favorite berries. Ursaring's hunger during this time makes it a ferocious danger.
217.name: Ursaring

218.description: Slugma does not have any blood in its body. Instead, intensely hot magma circulates throughout this Pokémon’s body, carrying essential nutrients and oxygen to its organs.
218.name: Slugma

219.description: Magcargo’s body temperature is approximately 18,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Water is vaporized on contact. If this Pokémon is caught in the rain, the raindrops instantly turn into steam, cloaking the area in a thick fog.
219.name: Magcargo

22.description: A Pokémon that dates back many years. If it senses danger, it flies high and away, instantly.
22.name: Fearow

220.description: Swinub excels at sniffing out mushrooms buried beneath grass or snow. Since ancient times, the people of Hisui have often relied upon this skill.
220.name: Swinub

221.description: The long fur of this Pokémon covers its eyes, ears, and even limbs, allowing Piloswine to resist harshly frigid conditions. The Pokémon's white tusks can be used to defeat its enemies.
221.name: Piloswine

222.description: These Pokémon live in warm seas. In prehistoric times, many lived in the oceans around the Galar region as well.
222.name: Corsola

223.description: Spits water from its mouth with incredible accuracy. It captures Burmy by shooting them down off the branches from which they dangle.
223.name: Remoraid

224.description: While Octillery still shoots water from its mouth, the drastic anatomical difference between it and Remoraid meant that for a long time, no one believed the former evolved from the latter.
224.name: Octillery

225.description: It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it’s always scrounging around for more food.
225.name: Delibird

226.description: This calm and gentle Pokémon swims gracefully through the sea. After building speed, it can leap out of the water. It is often misidentified as a bird Pokémon due to this behavior.
226.name: Mantine

227.description: People fashion swords from Skarmory’s shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.
227.name: Skarmory

228.description: They make repeated eerie howls before dawn to call attention to their pack.
228.name: Houndour

229.description: Identifiable by its eerie howls, people a long time ago thought it was the grim reaper and feared it.
229.name: Houndoom

23.description: The older it gets, the longer it grows. At night, it wraps its long body around tree branches to rest.
23.name: Ekans

230.description: Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they’ve been given to royalty as gifts.
230.name: Kingdra

231.description: Phanpy uses its long nose to shower itself. When others gather around, they thoroughly douse each other with water. These Pokémon can be seen drying their soaking-wet bodies at the edge of water.
231.name: Phanpy

232.description: If Donphan were to tackle with its hard body, even a house could be destroyed. Using its massive strength, the Pokémon helps clear rock and mud slides that block mountain trails.
232.name: Donphan

233.description: A bizarre item caused this Pokémon to evolve. While it now exhibits many new gestures and expressions, its biology remains inscrutable.
233.name: Porygon2

234.description: Its strangely shaped antlers have the power to bewitch those who see them. Medicine made by grinding up the black orbs from fallen antlers is an effective treatment for insomnia.
234.name: Stantler

235.description: It draws symbols with the fluid that oozes from the tip of its tail. Depending on the symbol, Smeargle fanatics will pay big money for them.
235.name: Smeargle

236.description: Even though it is small, it can’t be ignored because it will slug any handy target without warning.
236.name: Tyrogue

237.description: After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent’s timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.
237.name: Hitmontop

238.description: This is a very curious Pokémon. Smoochum decides what it likes and dislikes by touching things with its lips.
238.name: Smoochum

239.description: They generate electricity by spinning their arms. During a thunderstorm, if one hears the lively voices of children out in the wilderness, what one is actually hearing are the voices of Elekid.
239.name: Elekid

24.description: The frightening patterns on its belly have been studied. Six variations have been confirmed.
24.name: Arbok

240.description: This Pokémon lives in volcanic areas. With each breath, sparks spurt from its mouth and nose. When Magby is in good health, its flames gain a yellow tint.
240.name: Magby

241.description: This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.
241.name: Miltank

242.description: A kindhearted Pokémon that will care for any sick person or Pokémon until their health improves. The eggs it lays are delicious and bring good fortune to those who eat them.
242.name: Blissey

243.description: Raikou embodies the speed of lightning. The roars of this Pokémon send shock waves shuddering through the air and shake the ground as if lightning bolts had come crashing down.
243.name: Raikou

244.description: Entei embodies the passion of magma. This Pokémon is thought to have been born in the eruption of a volcano. It sends up massive bursts of fire that utterly consume all that they touch.
244.name: Entei

245.description: Suicune embodies the compassion of a pure spring of water. It runs across the land with gracefulness. This Pokémon has the power to purify dirty water.
245.name: Suicune

246.description: It feeds on soil. After it has eaten a large mountain, it will fall asleep so it can grow.
246.name: Larvitar

247.description: It will not stay still, even while it’s a pupa. It already has arms and legs under its solid shell.
247.name: Pupitar

248.description: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.
248.name: Tyranitar

249.description: Lugia’s wings pack devastating power—a light fluttering of its wings can blow apart regular houses. As a result, this Pokémon chooses to live out of sight deep under the sea.
249.name: Lugia

25.description: Possesses cheek sacs in which it stores electricity. This clever forest-dweller roasts tough berries with an electric shock before consuming them.
25.name: Pikachu

250.description: Ho-Oh’s feathers glow in seven colors depending on the angle at which they are struck by light. These feathers are said to bring happiness to the bearers. This Pokémon is said to live at the foot of a rainbow.
250.name: Ho-Oh

251.description: This Pokémon traveled through time to come from the future. It bolsters grass and trees with its own strength, and it can heal wounds, too.
251.name: Celebi

252.description: Treecko is cool, calm, and collected—it never panics under any situation. If a bigger foe were to glare at this Pokémon, it would glare right back without conceding an inch of ground.
252.name: Treecko

253.description: This Pokémon adeptly flies from branch to branch in trees. In a forest, no Pokémon can ever hope to catch a fleeing Grovyle however fast they may be.
253.name: Grovyle

254.description: Sceptile has seeds growing on its back. They are said to be bursting with nutrients that revitalize trees. This Pokémon raises the trees in a forest with loving care.
254.name: Sceptile

255.description: Torchic has a place inside its body where it keeps its flame. Give it a hug—it will be glowing with warmth. This Pokémon is covered all over by a fluffy coat of down.
255.name: Torchic

256.description: Combusken battles with the intensely hot flames it spews from its beak and with outstandingly destructive kicks. This Pokémon’s cry is very loud and distracting.
256.name: Combusken

257.description: Blaziken has incredibly strong legs—it can easily clear a 30-story building in one leap. This Pokémon’s blazing punches leave its foes scorched and blackened.
257.name: Blaziken

258.description: In water, Mudkip breathes using the gills on its cheeks. If it is faced with a tight situation in battle, this Pokémon will unleash its amazing power—it can crush rocks bigger than itself.
258.name: Mudkip

259.description: Marshtomp is much faster at traveling through mud than it is at swimming. This Pokémon’s hindquarters exhibit obvious development, giving it the ability to walk on just its hind legs.
259.name: Marshtomp

26.description: It can discharge bursts of electricity exceeding 100,000 volts— a single strike with that amount of power would incapacitate one of the Copperajah of my homeland.
26.name: Raichu

260.description: Swampert predicts storms by sensing subtle differences in the sounds of waves and tidal winds with its fins. If a storm is approaching, it piles up boulders to protect itself.
260.name: Swampert

261.description: Poochyena is an omnivore—it will eat anything. A distinguishing feature is how large its fangs are compared to its body. This Pokémon tries to intimidate its foes by making the hair on its tail bristle out.
261.name: Poochyena

262.description: Mightyena travel and act as a pack in the wild. The memory of its life in the wild compels the Pokémon to obey only those Trainers that it recognizes to possess superior skill.
262.name: Mightyena

263.description: Zigzagoon that adapted to regions outside Galar acquired this appearance. If you’ve lost something, this Pokémon can likely find it.
263.name: Zigzagoon

264.description: It uses its explosive speed and razor-sharp claws to bring down prey. Running along winding paths is not its strong suit.
264.name: Linoone

265.description: Likes sap and is abundant in the wild. Why it evolves into various different forms is unknown. One cannot tell from a Wurmple's appearance which form it will take when it evolves.
265.name: Wurmple

266.description: Wraps itself in thin strings of silk while it stores energy for evolution. It can't extend its limbs and its movement is slow, but its eyes keep a sharp lookout—Silcoon is always on guard.
266.name: Silcoon

267.description: A colorful and incredibly beautiful but also greedy Pokémon. In an effort to keep its favorite food all to itself, it will chase away Combee as they try to gather nectar.
267.name: Beautifly

268.description: The silk coating its body is thin but sufficiently strong. Cascoon's silk has a luster and texture superior to that of Silcoon's, and clothes made using Cascoon silk are regarded as top-notch.
268.name: Cascoon

269.description: Tends to be drawn to bonfires on dark nights. Difficult to chase away from settlements because of the way it scatters highly toxic scales.
269.name: Dustox

27.description: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.
27.name: Sandshrew

270.description: Its leaf grew too large for it to live on land. That is how it began to live floating in the water.
270.name: Lotad

271.description: It lives at the water’s edge where it is sunny. It sleeps on a bed of water grass by day and becomes active at night.
271.name: Lombre

272.description: If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.
272.name: Ludicolo

273.description: It attaches itself to a tree branch using the top of its head. Strong winds can sometimes make it fall.
273.name: Seedot

274.description: They live in holes bored in large trees. The sound of Nuzleaf’s grass flute fills listeners with dread.
274.name: Nuzleaf

275.description: It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.
275.name: Shiftry

276.description: Taillow is young—it has only just left its nest. As a result, it sometimes becomes lonesome and cries at night. This Pokémon feeds on Wurmple that live in forests.
276.name: Taillow

277.description: Swellow is very conscientious about the upkeep of its glossy wings. Once two Swellow are gathered, they diligently take care of cleaning each other’s wings.
277.name: Swellow

278.description: It soars on updrafts without flapping its wings. It makes a nest on sheer cliffs at the sea’s edge.
278.name: Wingull

279.description: Skimming the water’s surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.
279.name: Pelipper

28.description: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.
28.name: Sandslash

280.description: Tends to prefer people with a chipper disposition to those who are gloomy, but it has shown no discrimination with regard to age or gender. Needs more research.
280.name: Ralts

281.description: It resembles a maiden in appearance, but it wields strange powers to project visions of paradise. I suspect the crimson ornaments on its head are the key to its abilities.
281.name: Kirlia

282.description: It will dedicate itself to defending a master it has come to adore. Its pure white dress, reminiscent of those worn by ladies of nobility, is the dress of one who is willing to risk their life.
282.name: Gardevoir

283.description: It lives in ponds and marshes that feature lots of plant life. It often fights with Dewpider, whose habitat and diet are similar.
283.name: Surskit

284.description: Its thin, winglike antennae are highly absorbent. It waits out rainy days in tree hollows.
284.name: Masquerain

285.description: If Shroomish senses danger, it shakes its body and scatters spores from the top of its head. This Pokémon’s spores are so toxic, they make trees and weeds wilt.
285.name: Shroomish

286.description: The seeds ringing Breloom’s tail are made of hardened toxic spores. It is horrible to eat the seeds. Just taking a bite of this Pokémon’s seed will cause your stomach to rumble.
286.name: Breloom

287.description: Slakoth’s heart beats just once a minute. Whatever happens, it is content to loaf around motionless. It is rare to see this Pokémon in motion.
287.name: Slakoth

288.description: Vigoroth is simply incapable of remaining still. Even when it tries to sleep, the blood in its veins grows agitated, compelling this Pokémon to run wild throughout the jungle before it can settle down.
288.name: Vigoroth

289.description: Wherever Slaking live, rings of over a yard in diameter appear in grassy fields. They are made by the Pokémon as it eats all the grass within reach while lying prone on the ground.
289.name: Slaking

29.description: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran’s horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male’s horn.
29.name: Nidoran♀

290.description: It can sometimes live underground for more than 10 years. It absorbs nutrients from the roots of trees.
290.name: Nincada

291.description: This Pokémon is so quick, it is said to be able to avoid any attack. It loves to feed on tree sap.
291.name: Ninjask

292.description: A strange Pokémon—it flies without moving its wings, has a hollow shell for a body, and does not breathe.
292.name: Shedinja

293.description: When Whismur cries, the sound of its own voice startles it, making the Pokémon cry even louder. It cries until it’s exhausted, then it falls asleep.
293.name: Whismur

294.description: The force of this Pokémon’s loud voice isn’t just the sound—it’s also the wave of air pressure that blows opponents away and damages them.
294.name: Loudred

295.description: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it’ll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.
295.name: Exploud

296.description: There’s a rumor of a traditional recipe for stew that Trainers can use to raise strong Makuhita.
296.name: Makuhita

297.description: Hariyama that are big and fat aren’t necessarily strong. There are some small ones that move nimbly and use moves skillfully.
297.name: Hariyama

298.description: Although Azurill are normally docile, an angry one will swing around the big ball on its tail and try to smash its opponents.
298.name: Azurill

299.description: Once the people of Hisui discovered that its red nose always points north, they grew to rely on it greatly when traveling afar. The nose seems to work in a similar way to ancient compasses.
299.name: Nosepass

3.description: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.
3.name: Venusaur

30.description: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.
30.name: Nidorina

300.description: Skitty is known to chase around playfully after its own tail. In the wild, this Pokémon lives in holes in the trees of forests. It is very popular as a pet because of its adorable looks.
300.name: Skitty

301.description: Delcatty sleeps anywhere it wants without keeping a permanent nest. If other Pokémon approach it as it sleeps, this Pokémon will never fight—it will just move away somewhere else.
301.name: Delcatty

302.description: It feeds on gemstone crystals. In darkness, its eyes sparkle with the glitter of jewels.
302.name: Sableye

303.description: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.
303.name: Mawile

304.description: When Aron evolves, its steel armor peels off. In ancient times, people would collect Aron’s shed armor and make good use of it in their daily lives.
304.name: Aron

305.description: During territorial disputes, Lairon fight by slamming into each other. Close inspection of their steel armor reveals scratches and dents.
305.name: Lairon

306.description: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon’s strength.
306.name: Aggron

307.description: Meditite heightens its inner energy through meditation. It survives on just one berry a day. Minimal eating is another aspect of this Pokémon’s training.
307.name: Meditite

308.description: Through the power of meditation, Medicham developed its sixth sense. It gained the ability to use psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon is known to meditate for a whole month without eating.
308.name: Medicham

309.description: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.
309.name: Electrike

31.description: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.
31.name: Nidoqueen

310.description: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.
310.name: Manectric

311.description: When Plusle is cheering on its partner, it flashes with electric sparks from all over its body. If its partner loses, this Pokémon cries loudly.
311.name: Plusle

312.description: Minun loves to cheer on its partner in battle. It gives off sparks from its body while it is doing so. If its partner is in trouble, this Pokémon gives off increasing amounts of sparks.
312.name: Minun

313.description: Volbeat’s tail glows like a lightbulb. With other Volbeat, it uses its tail to draw geometric shapes in the night sky. This Pokémon loves the sweet aroma given off by Illumise.
313.name: Volbeat

314.description: Illumise leads a flight of illuminated Volbeat to draw signs in the night sky. This Pokémon is said to earn greater respect from its peers by composing more complex designs in the sky.
314.name: Illumise

315.description: Though beautiful, it has highly poisonous thorns. There is an old tradition in my homeland wherein one would send these thorns to an opponent to challenge them to a duel.
315.name: Roselia

316.description: Most of Gulpin’s body is made up of its stomach—its heart and brain are very small in comparison. This Pokémon’s stomach contains special enzymes that dissolve anything.
316.name: Gulpin

317.description: Swalot has no teeth, so what it eats, it swallows whole, no matter what. Its cavernous mouth yawns widely. An automobile tire could easily fit inside this Pokémon’s mouth.
317.name: Swalot

318.description: These Pokémon have sharp fangs and powerful jaws. Sailors avoid Carvanha dens at all costs.
318.name: Carvanha

319.description: This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sea. Any ship entering the waters Sharpedo calls home will be attacked—no exceptions.
319.name: Sharpedo

32.description: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.
32.name: Nidoran♂

320.description: When it sucks in a large volume of seawater, it becomes like a big, bouncy ball. It eats a ton of food daily.
320.name: Wailmer

321.description: Its immense size is the reason for its popularity. Wailord watching is a favorite sightseeing activity in various parts of the world.
321.name: Wailord

322.description: Numel stores magma of almost 2,200 degrees Fahrenheit within its body. If it gets wet, the magma cools and hardens. In that event, the Pokémon’s body grows heavy and its movements become sluggish.
322.name: Numel

323.description: The humps on Camerupt’s back are formed by a transformation of its bones. They sometimes blast out molten magma. This Pokémon apparently erupts often when it is enraged.
323.name: Camerupt

324.description: You find abandoned coal mines full of them. They dig tirelessly in search of coal.
324.name: Torkoal

325.description: Spoink keeps a pearl on top of its head. The pearl functions to amplify this Pokémon’s psychokinetic powers. It is therefore on a constant search for a bigger pearl.
325.name: Spoink

326.description: Grumpig uses the black pearls on its body to wield its fantastic powers. When it is doing so, it dances bizarrely. This Pokémon’s black pearls are valuable as works of art.
326.name: Grumpig

327.description: Each Spinda’s spot pattern is different. With its stumbling movements, it evades opponents’ attacks brilliantly!
327.name: Spinda

328.description: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.
328.name: Trapinch

329.description: To help make its wings grow, it dissolves quantities of prey in its digestive juices and guzzles them down every day.
329.name: Vibrava

33.description: It’s nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.
33.name: Nidorino

330.description: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.
330.name: Flygon

331.description: The more arid and harsh the environment, the more pretty and fragrant a flower Cacnea grows. This Pokémon battles by wildly swinging its thorny arms.
331.name: Cacnea

332.description: If a traveler is going through a desert in the thick of night, Cacturne will follow in a ragtag group. The Pokémon are biding their time, waiting for the traveler to tire and become incapable of moving.
332.name: Cacturne

333.description: Since Swablu looks like a cumulus cloud, foes can have a hard time finding it. Apparently its wings turned white over many generations.
333.name: Swablu

334.description: This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it’s provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.
334.name: Altaria

335.description: Zangoose usually stays on all fours, but when angered, it gets up on its hind legs and extends its claws. This Pokémon shares a bitter rivalry with Seviper that dates back over generations.
335.name: Zangoose

336.description: Seviper’s swordlike tail serves two purposes—it slashes foes and douses them with secreted poison. This Pokémon will not give up its long-running blood feud with Zangoose.
336.name: Seviper

337.description: It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.
337.name: Lunatone

338.description: Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.
338.name: Solrock

339.description: Makes its home in swamps with murky water. The poor visibility hides this Pokémon from predators, and the slime on its body makes grasping it difficult.
339.name: Barboach

34.description: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.
34.name: Nidoking

340.description: Strikes its caudal fin against the swamp bed to shake the ground and startle its prey. It will then swallow the fleeing prey whole. People mistook this behavior as the cause of earthquakes.
340.name: Whiscash

341.description: It was originally a Pokémon from afar that escaped to the wild. It can adapt to the dirtiest river.
341.name: Corphish

342.description: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.
342.name: Crawdaunt

343.description: It was discovered in ancient ruins. While moving, it constantly spins. It stands on one foot even when asleep.
343.name: Baltoy

344.description: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.
344.name: Claydol

345.description: Lileep clings to rocks on the seabed. When prey comes close, this Pokémon entangles it with petallike tentacles.
345.name: Lileep

346.description: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.
346.name: Cradily

347.description: Anorith can swim swiftly by pulling its eight wings through the water like oars on a boat. This Pokémon is an ancestor of modern bug Pokémon.
347.name: Anorith

348.description: Though it lives on land, it’s also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.
348.name: Armaldo

349.description: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.
349.name: Feebas

35.description: It can be found in quiet mountain areas on a full moon's night. Its dancing and its tiny, faintly glowing wings confer upon it a lovely fairylike quality.
35.name: Clefairy

350.description: It’s said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you’re feeling.
350.name: Milotic

351.description: Its form changes depending on the weather. The rougher conditions get, the rougher Castform’s disposition!
351.name: Castform

352.description: Its color changes for concealment and also when its mood or health changes. The darker the color, the healthier it is.
352.name: Kecleon

353.description: There’s a proverb that says, “Shun the house where Shuppet gather in the growing dusk.”
353.name: Shuppet

354.description: Resentment at being cast off made it spring into being. Some say that treating it well will satisfy it, and it will once more become a stuffed toy.
354.name: Banette

355.description: I've heard that the children of Hisui all begin to behave once they've been told the story of how this Pokémon roams about before the witching hour to spirit away misbehaving children.
355.name: Duskull

356.description: There are rumors that peeking inside its bandage-wrapped body will cause one to get pulled in through the gaps between the bandages, never to return. I've been too scared to verify.
356.name: Dusclops

357.description: Bunches of delicious fruit grow around its neck. In warm areas, many ranches raise Tropius.
357.name: Tropius

358.description: Can emit waves of air powerful enough to knock out prey taller than itself. I hypothesize that it amplifies the faint sound of wind within its body.
358.name: Chimecho

359.description: Because of this Pokémon’s ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.
359.name: Absol

36.description: Legend says that on clear, quiet nights, it listens for the voices of its kin living on the moon. I, too, often think of my homeland, so far away.
36.name: Clefable

360.description: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.
360.name: Wynaut

361.description: Arrives alongside the first snow. It's thought that homes Snorunt visit will prosper for many generations. By tradition, one might offer a lump of ice made from pure water at one's front door.
361.name: Snorunt

362.description: It covers its body with an armor of ice harder than steel. Uses its breath to freeze prey, which it then devours as if they were frozen desserts.
362.name: Glalie

363.description: During the season when drift ice approaches the shore, Spheal prefers living on the ice—where fewer predators lurk—rather than the land. Its fur retains heat superbly and resists harsh cold.
363.name: Spheal

364.description: Its white whiskers are very sensitive. Sealeo will balance Spheal on the tip of its nose, checking its scent and its feel to be sure the Spheal is healthy.
364.name: Sealeo

365.description: Its thick tusks are strong enough to shatter drift ice. They have been known to break, but they will grow back by the next year. The Hisui region is well known for these broken tusks.
365.name: Walrein

366.description: Clamperl’s pearls are exceedingly precious. They can be more than 10 times as costly as Shellder’s pearls.
366.name: Clamperl

367.description: Deep seas are their habitat. According to tradition, when Huntail wash up onshore, something unfortunate will happen.
367.name: Huntail

368.description: It sucks bodily fluids out of its prey. The leftover meat sinks to the seafloor, where it becomes food for other Pokémon.
368.name: Gorebyss

369.description: This Pokémon was discovered during deep-sea exploration. Its appearance hasn’t changed in 100,000,000 years, so it’s called a living fossil.
369.name: Relicanth

37.description: In its belly burns a fire, which Vulpix spits out in the form of fireballs. When young, this Pokémon has but one white tail. As the Pokémon matures, this single tail splits into six.
37.name: Vulpix

370.description: Luvdisc makes its home in coral reefs in warm seas. It especially likes sleeping in the space between Corsola’s branches.
370.name: Luvdisc

371.description: Bagon is a solitary Pokémon that doesn’t form groups with others of its kind. It also has a head hard enough to cleave a boulder in one strike.
371.name: Bagon

372.description: Shelgon ignores its hunger entirely, never eating any food. Apparently, Shelgon will evolve once all its energy stores are used up.
372.name: Shelgon

373.description: While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.
373.name: Salamence

374.description: The cells in this Pokémon’s body are composed of magnetic material. Instead of blood, magnetic forces flow through Beldum’s body.
374.name: Beldum

375.description: Using magnetic forces to stay aloft, this Pokémon flies at high speeds, weaving through harsh mountain terrain in pursuit of prey.
375.name: Metang

376.description: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.
376.name: Metagross

377.description: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon’s rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.
377.name: Regirock

378.description: This Pokémon’s body is made of solid ice. It’s said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.
378.name: Regice

379.description: It’s rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet’s mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.
379.name: Registeel

38.description: The coat of gleaming golden fur is quite magnificent. This species is said to store sacred power in its nine long tails and to live for a millennium.
38.name: Ninetales

380.description: Latias is highly intelligent and capable of understanding human speech. It is covered with a glass-like down. The Pokémon enfolds its body with its down and refracts light to alter its appearance.
380.name: Latias

381.description: Latios will only open its heart to a Trainer with a compassionate spirit. This Pokémon can fly faster than a jet plane by folding its forelegs to minimize air resistance.
381.name: Latios

382.description: Kyogre is said to be the personification of the sea itself. Legends tell of its many clashes against Groudon, as each sought to gain the power of nature.
382.name: Kyogre

383.description: Through Primal Reversion and with nature’s full power, it will take back its true form. It can cause magma to erupt and expand the landmass of the world.
383.name: Groudon

384.description: It flies forever through the ozone layer, consuming meteoroids for sustenance. The many meteoroids in its body provide the energy it needs to Mega Evolve.
384.name: Rayquaza

385.description: It’s believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.
385.name: Jirachi

386.description: Deoxys emerged from a virus that came from space. It is highly intelligent and wields psychokinetic powers. This Pokémon shoots lasers from the crystalline organ on its chest.
386.name: Deoxys

387.description: This Pokémon becomes more energetic the more sunlight there is. The part resembling a shell is similar to silt and is slightly damp and warm to the touch.
387.name: Turtwig

388.description: Appears where there is clean spring water. The fruit that grows on the shrubs on its shell is sweet, nutritious, and truly delicious.
388.name: Grotle

389.description: This remarkable, large-bodied Pokémon would serve beautifully as borrowed scenery for a garden, and its strength is peerless. Torterra roams the wilderness in search of clean water.
389.name: Torterra

39.description: By freely changing the wavelength of its voice, Jigglypuff sings a mysterious melody sure to make any listener sleepy.
39.name: Jigglypuff

390.description: Full of vigor and always in high spirits. It was once known by the name ”Lantern-Tail” and feared as some kind of apparition.
390.name: Chimchar

391.description: The deeper the blue on its face, the more powerful it will grow to become. It leaps about every which way and lands powerful blows against its opponents with the flame on its tail.
391.name: Monferno

392.description: A tall, hardy Pokémon with a dazzling appearance. It shrouds itself in flame and battles as if engaged in dance—truly a sight to behold.
392.name: Infernape

393.description: Prefers cold climes and appears along coasts. It's an adorable little thing—as cute as any child—but it's also prideful, unwilling to accept handouts from people.
393.name: Piplup

394.description: It swims gracefully through the frigid sea and sings with a voice like the roaring tide. It has powerful, sturdy wings and dignity to match.
394.name: Prinplup

395.description: Since ancient times, it has been revered by the people of Hisui, who call it the Master of the Waves. Its wings are a match for even master-crafted blades.
395.name: Empoleon

396.description: They live in the fields and mountains, gathering in large flocks. Their cries are quite obnoxious. Though small, their wings are strong—a strike from them leaves pain that persists for a week.
396.name: Starly

397.description: They form remarkably large flocks and are constantly fighting amongst themselves. I suspect that those with magnificent plumes on their heads are the strong ones.
397.name: Staravia

398.description: It has left the flock, having gained strength enough to survive on its own. The astounding force with which Staraptor flies through the air allows it to carry away large, burly targets.
398.name: Staraptor

399.description: Bidoof has an unsophisticated face and is rarely flustered by anything. There have been incidents involving Bidoof sauntering into villages and gnawing on the houses without a single care.
399.name: Bidoof

4.description: From the time it is born, a flame burns at the tip of its tail. Its life would end if the flame were to go out.
4.name: Charmander

40.description: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.
40.name: Wigglytuff

400.description: Bibarel fur repels water and is also a fantastic material for heat retention. These Pokémon create dams on rivers to live in.
400.name: Bibarel

401.description: When the trees take on new hues, more of these Pokémon appear. The tone they create by striking their antennae together resembles that of the marimba, an instrument of foreign lands.
401.name: Kricketot

402.description: It uses its cutlass-like arms to produce sound, the melody of which varies from individual to individual. It is a worthwhile endeavor to seek out one's favorite tunes.
402.name: Kricketune

403.description: Shakes its body to generate electricity. Its stature belies its aggression—one must be patient to tame this Pokémon.
403.name: Shinx

404.description: Proudly uses its electrified claws as weapons. It seems to be a gracious Pokémon, evenly sharing the spoils of the hunt with others of its kind.
404.name: Luxio

405.description: They form packs, each having one male as leader. Legends say that when Luxray's two eyes shimmer with gold, the Pokémon can see through anything.
405.name: Luxray

406.description: When the sun's light strengthens, the bud atop this Pokémon's head opens. This is a sign to the people that the harsh winter is over, and the season of budding has begun.
406.name: Budew

407.description: Hidden within the bouquet on each hand are thorned whips loaded with virulent poison. Roserade moves gracefully as it corners its prey and mercilessly lashes them with its whips.
407.name: Roserade

408.description: An incredibly rare sight. They duel each other by ramming their heads together, and the resulting sound echoes throughout the area like the pealing of a bell.
408.name: Cranidos

409.description: Very little is known about its biology. Can knock down massive trees by smashing its beautiful, pearl-like crown against them.
409.name: Rampardos

41.description: Makes its home in gloomy caves. Atrophied eyes have left this Pokémon blind, so it scans its surroundings via sound waves that it emits from its mouth as it flies.
41.name: Zubat

410.description: Much remains unknown about this Pokémon, as few have ever seen it. However, we know that it is calm and dislikes conflict, and it enjoys polishing its face against trees and rocks.
410.name: Shieldon

411.description: Its face is sturdy—as strong as diamond—and this hardness offers a very stable defense. Much about this species is still unknown, such as its natural habitat.
411.name: Bastiodon

412.description: If its cloak is even slightly damaged, Burmy will immediately repair it with whatever is close at hand. The Pokémon within the cloak is scrawny and vulnerable to the cold.
412.name: Burmy

413.description: When Burmy evolved, its cloak became a part of this Pokémon’s body. The cloak is never shed.
413.name: Wormadam

414.description: Scatters steel-colored scales as it flaps its wings. Despite being observed feeding primarily on the nectar of flowers, Mothim is not often seen around flower gardens.
414.name: Mothim

415.description: They swear fealty to a queen Pokémon and work diligently to gather nectar. Each swarm produces a different flavor of honey.
415.name: Combee

416.description: Commands its subjects to build its hive. It will dispatch any interlopers who dare sneak into its nest and use them as nourishment for itself.
416.name: Vespiquen

417.description: A species related to the Pikachu line. Though Pachirisu is a calm Pokémon, it still presents a danger should one touch its electrified tail or cheeks.
417.name: Pachirisu

418.description: It moves freely in the water by spinning its forked tail for propulsion. The resemblance to the screw of a steamboat is coincidental.
418.name: Buizel

419.description: Has a long, rather splendid flotation sac, which prevents Floatzel from drowning even in stormy seas. One might glimpse this species around fishing hamlets from time to time.
419.name: Floatzel

42.description: It sinks its sharp fangs into other creatures and slurps up their blood. A closer look at the fangs reveals that they are hollow and akin to straws.
42.name: Golbat

420.description: Once the fruit growing alongside the main body is large and plump, Cherubi will use the nutrients within to evolve. The fruit then detaches, becoming nourishment for other creatures.
420.name: Cherubi

421.description: Motionless, save for the occasional quiver. A rich array of Pokémon can be found gathered around it, drawn by the scent exuded from Cherrim's folded petals.
421.name: Cherrim

422.description: Found in abundance on seashores bordering warm waters. Shellos are unexpectedly friendly and will crawl toward any person they see. Take care not to get coated in mucus!
422.name: Shellos

423.description: Eats beach sand for nourishment. Should one Gastrodon encounter another of a different color, a fierce battle will inevitably ensue.
423.name: Gastrodon

424.description: To affirm their kinship, members of this species will form a ring by linking their newly doubled tails together. On rare occasions, humans have been accepted into such rings.
424.name: Ambipom

425.description: Said to lure away young children and carry them off to the afterlife. Some whisper that Drifloon are formed of reincarnated human souls, but these rumors are as yet unconfirmed.
425.name: Drifloon

426.description: It drifts along at dusk, perfectly silent. Its transient, melancholy aspect touches some people deeply—every so often, one will come upon a song or poem devoted to Drifblim.
426.name: Drifblim

427.description: My hypothesis as to why Buneary rolls up its ears is that its hearing is far too keen. I surmise that the Pokémon protects its hearing by limiting the sound that may enter its ears.
427.name: Buneary

428.description: Its fur is warm and yet remarkably light. This Pokémon kicks as though it were a master of karate, driving back its opponents with ease.
428.name: Lopunny

429.description: The incantations Mismagius chants can ward against misfortune, so a custom exists of inviting it into one's home. Incur the Pokémon's displeasure, however, and disaster will surely ensue.
429.name: Mismagius

43.description: During the day, it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun. It grows by bathing in moonlight.
43.name: Oddish

430.description: One cry from this Pokémon, and a murder of Murkrow come flying. At such times, one would think the curtain of night had fallen, plunging the world into jet-black darkness.
430.name: Honchkrow

431.description: Bewitches humans with its helical tail and piercing gaze. Its hidden claws are quite sharp as well, making this Pokémon an exceedingly tricky opponent if antagonized.
431.name: Glameow

432.description: Though impudent and difficult to tame, Purugly enjoys great popularity due to its fur, the beauty of which surpasses even velveteen.
432.name: Purugly

433.description: This Pokémon gave me an excruciating headache when it seemingly cried out without making a sound. Perhaps there are some sounds that the human ear is simply incapable of hearing.
433.name: Chingling

434.description: The poison that gushes from its aft end is accompanied by an utterly evil-smelling odor with such potency that one whiff can induce memory loss.
434.name: Stunky

435.description: Sprays a poisonous fluid to take down prey. Sometimes, unable to stomach the stench of its own fluid, it leaves the bested prey uneaten.
435.name: Skuntank

436.description: Floats using a mysterious energy. The pattern engraved upon its back is held as sacred and can sometimes be found in imagery from ancient cemeteries and other such timeworn places.
436.name: Bronzor

437.description: Some believe that its bell-like cry opens holes to another world. It has been revered as a deity since ancient times.
437.name: Bronzong

438.description: Its tears elicit sympathy from those who see them, but do not be deceived! This expulsion of body water is merely a physiological mechanism for keeping itself in good health.
438.name: Bonsly

439.description: Known to turn up in bustling marketplaces now and again. It mimics people much as a child would, then watches how they react, eyes sparkling.
439.name: Mime Jr.

44.description: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.
44.name: Gloom

440.description: In imitation of Chansey, it keeps a round stone tucked into its belly pouch and cherishes it dearly. It gets along well with children and will sometimes play house with them for fun.
440.name: Happiny

441.description: A versatile performer skilled in the imitation of human speech. It is said that older, more experienced Chatot can even understand the meaning of the words they mimic.
441.name: Chatot

442.description: It lays curses by thinking wicked thoughts. Writings tell that this Pokémon was born out of the assembly of five score and eight malevolent spirits.
442.name: Spiritomb

443.description: It nests in caves untouched by sunlight. Its sharp teeth may fall out when worn away or after an impact, but they regrow within a few days.
443.name: Gible

444.description: Though Gabite are usually of a violent disposition, when I gave one a glass bead it had been eyeing covetously, it suddenly became quite docile.
444.name: Gabite

445.description: Soars across the heavens at blinding speed—a magnificent sight! It has a feral disposition. Utmost caution is required if one meets a Garchomp out in the wilds.
445.name: Garchomp

446.description: Its robust stomach allows it to nonchalantly devour even rotted matter. It pays frequent visits to villages, seeking out food scraps intended for compost.
446.name: Munchlax

447.description: Though infantile in appearance, it has the mysterious ability to read the minds of humans. The pure of heart are met with Riolu's approval, while those of ill nature earn only its loathing.
447.name: Riolu

448.description: A most gallant-looking creature. It emits energy waves and controls them with precision, using them to sense even faraway beings. I have given the name ”aura” to this power.
448.name: Lucario

449.description: Though large and languid, Hippopotas is difficult to detect due to its tendency to burrow into and lurk beneath the soil. When agitated or excited, it expels sand from its nostrils.
449.name: Hippopotas

45.description: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.
45.name: Vileplume

450.description: Short-tempered and easily moved to violence. It whips up whirlwinds of sand to crush its foes' spirits, then goes in for the attack.
450.name: Hippowdon

451.description: Its claws are not only razor-sharp but poisonous, making Skorupi a highly dangerous Pokémon. It seems to be weakened by cold temperatures, however.
451.name: Skorupi

452.description: Has a brutish, ferocious temperament. With immense strength and a sturdy shell off which swords will bounce, it rampages about and wreaks havoc.
452.name: Drapion

453.description: A poison wielder with a dastardly personality. Despite such qualities, this species is afforded a measure of popularity due to its peculiar cry and comical features.
453.name: Croagunk

454.description: Its crimson claws contain a virulent toxin. This toxin can be made into a tonic by diluting it, mixing it with several types of wild grass, and boiling it down over two days.
454.name: Toxicroak

455.description: Though this is a plant Pokémon, it has a gluttonous and unruly temperament. Carnivine attacks its prey with its cavernous maw wide open.
455.name: Carnivine

456.description: What a gorgeous sight this Pokémon is as it swims with its long, pink-painted caudal fins fluttering behind it. Finneon's beautiful appearance has led to its nickname: ”finery fish.”
456.name: Finneon

457.description: Uses its gleaming fins to hunt its prey. The view of Lumineon schooling near the surface of the sea at night is breathtaking— it's as though there were shining stars right there.
457.name: Lumineon

458.description: Though ball-like in shape, this Pokémon is a proficient swimmer. I have discovered that if a Mantyke spends much time with schools of Remoraid, it will eventually achieve evolution.
458.name: Mantyke

459.description: One is likely to encounter this Pokémon while out in the snow. There are stories of Snover appearing in human settlements but doing no harm—rather, they bond with the children.
459.name: Snover

46.description: Sometimes seen at the foot of trees in humid forests. The mushrooms on its back—called tochukaso—are not present on infant specimens and instead emerge as Paras matures.
46.name: Paras

460.description: A powerful Pokémon that can split huge boulders with ease. Dislikes associating with others and chooses to live quietly deep within the mountains, playing with the snow.
460.name: Abomasnow

461.description: This species corners prey as a pack, under the guidance of a leader. Weavile displays increased cunning, leading me to speculate that its evolution caused further brain development.
461.name: Weavile

462.description: I theorize that a special magnetic field influenced this Pokémon, changing its molecular structure and causing it to evolve. It emits strange radio waves toward space from its antenna.
462.name: Magnezone

463.description: Its tongue can extend and contract freely, and it is capable of reaching lengths over 10 times Lickilicky's height. Beware of the saliva, as it contains corrosive elements.
463.name: Lickilicky

464.description: This Pokémon evolved through use of a curious item. Its rocklike hide is composed of a mysterious substance and can withstand a blow from a masterwork sword with nary a scratch.
464.name: Rhyperior

465.description: Draped with long vines, it resembles a shrub in appearance. It swings bundles of vines as though they were arms, wrapping them around prey to ensnare them.
465.name: Tangrowth

466.description: Its evolution was induced by an unusual item, and its electrical output rises along with its heart rate. From its tails, it can unleash an electric current measuring 20,000 volts.
466.name: Electivire

467.description: Use of a strange item caused this Pokémon to evolve. Fireballs launched from the ends of its tubelike arms are hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant.
467.name: Magmortar

468.description: Scant few have ever sighted this Pokémon. After studying what literature remains, I am certain Togekiss will reveal itself when peace reigns in the land.
468.name: Togekiss

469.description: Extremely violent. When hunting, it wastes none of its energy, aiming only for prey's most vulnerable spots. Any who manage to tame this Pokémon must be of incredible bravery.
469.name: Yanmega

47.description: Mushroom-lacking specimens of this Pokémon lie unmoving in the forest, lending credence to the hypothesis that the large mushroom is in control of Parasect's actions.
47.name: Parasect

470.description: Cells similar to those of plants have been found in its fur. Its hard tail can fell a large tree with one stroke, and the tail's sharpness exceeds even that of a sword crafted by a master.
470.name: Leafeon

471.description: Glaceon is able to lower its body temperature very quickly. It freezes the atmosphere, creating diamond dust that glitters like gems while it flutters and dances around.
471.name: Glaceon

472.description: It glides soundlessly on pitch-black wings and sinks sharp fangs into the throat of its prey. It takes on a look of satisfaction once it has entirely drained its prey of blood.
472.name: Gliscor

473.description: This species reached its zenith during the period known as the ice age. I suspect that Hisui's frigid climate is in harmony with Mamoswine's constitution, thus awakening hidden potential.
473.name: Mamoswine

474.description: A curious item induced this evolution. The Pokémon's offensive capabilities have greatly increased, but the strangeness of its behavior has magnified in equal measure. This worries me.
474.name: Porygon-Z

475.description: The blades extending from its elbows are sharper than the finest swords. Its swordsmanship, albeit self-taught, is astonishingly impressive.
475.name: Gallade

476.description: It is able to emit powerful magnetism, allowing it control over the iron sand that forms its luscious mustache. Using this iron sand, Probopass forms hard stones with which it smites its prey.
476.name: Probopass
